nvitk.measure.morpho.anatomy.nearest_dist_to_vessel_names(vessel_names: List[str], pt_mm: numpy.ndarray, multilabel: numpy.ndarray, spacing, mapping: dict) → float¶

nvitk.measure.morpho.anatomy.anatomical_endpoint_score(pt_mm: numpy.ndarray, rule: str | None, axes: nvitk.measure.morpho.anatomy_axes.AnatomicalAxes | None = None) → float¶

Ranking score for pt_mm under an anatomical direction rule (lower = more extreme in that direction).

With axes the rule is resolved against the volume’s real orientation and the subject’s species (see nvitk.measure.morpho.anatomy_axes). Without it the legacy hardcoded axes are used: array axis 2 = S/I, axis 1 = A/P, axis 0 increasing toward L — i.e. an implicit LAS volume.

nvitk.measure.morpho.anatomy.orient_centerline_points_by_flow(pts: numpy.ndarray, vessel_info: nvitk.measure.morpho.models.VesselInfo, multilabel: numpy.ndarray, spacing, mapping: dict, axes: nvitk.measure.morpho.anatomy_axes.AnatomicalAxes | None = None) → Tuple[numpy.ndarray, bool]¶

Orient a centerline so it runs upstream→downstream per vessel_info flow topology.

Returns (points, was_reversed). Falls back through downstream-only, then upstream-only proximity when one side of the topology is unavailable, and finally onto the vessel’s no_upstream_start anatomical rule. That last fallback matters for root vessels whose topology has no usable flow_from/flow_to ("systemic" upstream, empty downstream) — e.g. every entry in mouse_root_topology.json — which otherwise get no orientation at all when the component is unbranched.
